label: def:bring-cone-tetraplectic-structure
title: Tetraplectic structure on the affine cone $C(\mathcal{B})$ over Bring's curve
html:
Definition. Tetraplectic structure on the affine cone C(\mathcal{B}) over Bring's curve

Let \mathcal{B} \subset \mathbb{P}^4 be Bring's surface — the genus-4 curve cut out by the vanishing of the first three power sums, with maximal automorphism group S_5. Its affine cone is the affine variety

  C(\mathcal{B})
  \;=\;
  \Bigl\{\, x \in \mathbb{C}^5 \;:\;
    \textstyle\sum_j x_j = \sum_j x_j^2 = \sum_j x_j^3 = 0 \,\Bigr\}
  \;\subset\; \mathbb{C}^5,

a complex surface, hence a real 4-manifold. Write M = C(\mathcal{B}).

On a 4m-dimensional manifold, a tetraplectic structure [foth2002] is a closed 4-form \Omega \in \Omega^4(M) whose m-th power \Omega^m is a non-degenerate volume form. Here m = 1: every 4-form on a 4-manifold is closed, so d\Omega = 0 is automatic and the tetraplectic requirement reduces to a nowhere-vanishing volume form.

M inherits the discrete symmetries of \mathcal{B} — an S_5 \times \mathbb{Z}_2 action, with \mathbb{Z}_2 generated by an involution \tau. Averaging an arbitrary initial volume form \omega_0 over that action,

  \Omega
  \;=\;
  \frac{1}{|S_5|} \sum_{g \in S_5}
    \bigl( \omega_0 \pm \tau^{*}(g^{*}\omega_0) \bigr),

produces an S_5-invariant tetraplectic volume form \Omega. Fix it, and set the state space to be \mathcal{H} = L^2(M, \Omega).

Because \Omega is S_5-invariant, \mathcal{H} carries a unitary S_5 action and so decomposes into orthogonal isotypic components indexed by the integer partitions of 5. This is the entry point to the rest of the chapter: the continuous geometry of the cone is resolved into the same Young-diagram data that indexes the Wedderburn blocks elsewhere in the framework.
